State-space models

Source: R/state-space.R
ctrl_ss.Rd

Construct a linear time-invariant state-space model $$\dot x(t) = A x(t) + B u(t), \quad y(t) = C x(t) + D u(t)$$ in continuous time, or $$x_{k+1} = A x_k + B u_k, \quad y_k = C x_k + D u_k$$ in discrete time with sample interval dt.

Usage

ctrl_ss(
  A,
  B = NULL,
  C = NULL,
  D = NULL,
  dt = NULL,
  state_names = NULL,
  input_names = NULL,
  output_names = NULL
)

Arguments

A

State matrix (n x n).

B

Input matrix (n x m).

C

Output matrix (p x n).

D

Feedthrough matrix (p x m); defaults to zero.

dt

NULL or 0 for continuous time, or a positive sample interval.

state_names

Optional unique state names.

input_names

Optional unique input names.

output_names

Optional unique output names. Defaults are x1, x2, ..., u1, ... and y1, ....

Value

An object of class c("ctrl_ss", "ctrl_system").

Details

The time domain is explicit: dt = NULL or dt = 0 gives a continuous time model, and a positive dt gives a discrete time model sampled every dt time units. There is no "unknown sample time"; discrete models always carry their sample interval.

Matrices are validated for finiteness and for consistent dimensions: A is n x n, B is n x m, C is p x n and D is p x m. D defaults to a zero matrix. A model with n = 0 is a static gain y = D u; pass A = NULL together with D, or use ctrl_gain(). Scalars are accepted for 1 x 1 matrices and vectors for single-row or single-column matrices only when the shape is unambiguous.

See also

ctrl_tf(), ctrl_ssdata(), ctrl_c2d(), ctrl_poles()

Examples

A <- matrix(c(0, 1, -2, -3), 2, byrow = TRUE)
plant <- ctrl_ss(A, B = c(0, 1), C = c(1, 0))
plant
#> State-space model (continuous time)
#> 2 states, 1 inputs, 1 outputs
#> 
#> A =
#>    x1 x2
#> x1  0  1
#> x2 -2 -3
#> 
#> B =
#>    u1
#> x1  0
#> x2  1
#> 
#> C =
#>    x1 x2
#> y1  1  0
#> 
#> D =
#>    u1
#> y1  0
ctrl_poles(plant)
#> [1] -1+0i -2+0i

# A discrete time model sampled every 0.1 time units
ctrl_ss(0.9, 0.1, 1, dt = 0.1)
#> State-space model (discrete time, dt = 0.1)
#> 1 states, 1 inputs, 1 outputs
#> 
#> A =
#>     x1
#> x1 0.9
#> 
#> B =
#>     u1
#> x1 0.1
#> 
#> C =
#>    x1
#> y1  1
#> 
#> D =
#>    u1
#> y1  0
